name: Chantries of the Usurpers (Libellus Sanguinis II Lore)

text.content: Deep within the Carpathian mountains, Ceoris was once the heart of the Hermetic Order of magi who would become Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}, and it now occupies a central position in the clan's affairs. Its stone walls, steeped in the magic of the land itself, have survived wave after wave of assault from the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} and other supernatural enemies that haunt those desolate peaks through a combination of magical and physical defenses whose details are closely guarded. From his sanctum in the fortress's bowels, Goratrix discovered the means of the clan's transformation from mortal magi to immortal Cainites and created the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.qfOm4Ua1XRKsv8bU]{Gargoyles} that turned the tide of the war against the Tzimisce. Tremere himself is believed to sleep somewhere within Ceoris, while Etrius, one of the original seven who underwent the transformation alongside him, serves as the unceasing guardian of the slumbering Antediluvian.

Just outside the English city of Durham, within sight of the cathedral housing some of the isle's holiest relics, stands a Roman-era tower serving as a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} chantry. Its resident, the elder Meerlinda, chose the site in part for its proximity to Glastonbury and its legends of the Holy Grail, and has fortified it with magical wards and underground passages built by her ghoul servants. Remote from the interference of Prince Mithras and the affairs of London, the Durham chantry allows the Tremere of Britain to gather strength quietly before expanding into Scotland and Ireland.

Once head of the chantry at Ceoris, Goratrix now leads Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}'s expansion into France from a chantry near the university district of Paris. He and his followers have constructed an underground labyrinth to dissuade unwanted visitors, and his Gargoyle servitors act as guards, defenders, and spies throughout the city. Goratrix's ongoing studies of the vampiric form, conducted largely upon unwilling human and Cainite "toys," have made the Paris chantry one of the clan's strongest centers of scholarly research — and one of its most quietly feared.

Invited into Austria by the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} to help secure their hold on the region, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} established the Vienna chantry only recently, overseen personally by Etrius. Its defenses remain a closely held secret even within the clan, and its library reportedly rivals the one at Ceoris itself, making it an increasingly important center of Tremere scholarship in the Holy Roman Empire.

The strangest of the clan's chantries lies near Riga in Lithuania, home to the Telyavelic @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} or "Telyavs" — a small, pagan branch of the clan named for Telyavel, the Lithuanian god of the dead. Unable to accept the horror of their transformation, this group left Ceoris ostensibly to spread Tremere influence but in truth to seek some means of reversing what had been done to them; along the way they developed Sielanic Thaumaturgy, a nature- and spirit-based tradition the wider clan regards with suspicion as a possible offshoot of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} koldunic sorcery. The Telyavs remain only loosely connected to the rest of the clan and share little of their findings, prompting quiet worry among other Tremere that the bloodline walks a dangerous path outside the pyramid's authority. Historically, the Telyavelic Tremere are wiped out by the 16th century when the union of Lithuania and Poland brings the triumph of Christianity and the Inquisition's fires to their chantry near Riga.

vtmlarp.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book Two: Usurpers
